Issued at 358 AM EDT Tue Sep 1 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Broad pattern has ridging over the CONUS/North America, particular, 
the eastern half...with +2 standard deviations from the mean upper 
ridge over Hudson Bay...and similarly anomalous southern stream 
ridge centered over the Mid MS Valley. A 554dm 500mb low is plowing 
its way through the ridge axis attm, currently spinning over central 
Manitoba, with a strong height rise/fall couplet across southern 
Canada associated with this...and very occluded 1000mb surface low 
smack dab beneath the upper low, with a surface cold front 
stretching down into the central Plains. Very warm and sticky ahead 
of this front, with dewpoints largely in the 70s across WI and much 
of northern Lower south of a stagnant stationary front stretching 
from western Lake Superior through the Straits and toward New York 
and the Mid-Atlantic; pwat on our 0z sounding was 1.66in. Lots of 
fog/low-clouds continue to hang out near and north of the stationary 
boundary across the Yoop and parts of the Straits/Tip of the Mitt. 
Very warm airmass in place, characterized by 700mb temps around +10-
12C, and freezing levels of 15kft on our 0z/01 sounding. Attm, low-
level jet is stronger to our northwest nearer to the upper low, and 
to our southeast across SE MI. Approximately 2000J/kg CAPE on our 
evening sounding, with some minor CINH, which is generally 
representative of the region attm...the bulk of which is going 
untapped as of 4z, with little in the way of forcing in the region 
attm. 

Upper low looks to track just to our north through Wednesday, 
weakening to some extent as it does so, dragging a boundary into the 
area and leaving it for a while. Upstream, broad upper low digs into 
the PacNW, resulting in ridge axis generally strengthening over the 
Central Plains/Upper Midwest later this week, which should bring 
warm advection and some potential convection to the Upper MS Valley 
through the end of the week. We should remain largely in the 
vicinity of aforementioned lingering baroclinic zone through the 
remainder of the week, and thus, hold onto the threat of periodic 
unsettled weather into the start of the holiday weekend -- much of 
which may be dependent on how early/late day convection evolves 
(i.e., higher uncertainty than usual). Some uncertainty in the 
evolution of the northern stream pattern across central Canada this 
weekend, depending on a lobe of energy crossing the top of the 
ridge, and whether or not the ridge is able to block northern 
Canadian energy from sinking southward into eastern Canada for early 
next week. This could mean the difference between a slightly warmer 
end to the Labor Day weekend...or a warmer and slightly more active 
one. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm potential the next few days...With signals for the 
boundary to drape in today, and that PV max to slide by just to our 
north...not impossible there could be enough forcing around to pop 
something today. Relatively light low-level flow also suggests lake 
breezes will come into play, particularly across northern Lower MI, 
which could play a role in boosting pop-up showers/storms, 
especially this afternoon. If we end up clearing out today, 
certainly possible the cap could be broken as well, with potential 
for 1500-3000J/kg CAPE here, given weak stability aloft. Think this 
idea will depend on what happens yet this morning, and there is some 
potential for activity to develop prior to 12z, though forcing will 
not be super great. Deep layer shear should pick up early this 
morning as the nose of the 500mb jet enters the region, and will 
remain at or above 40kts through the day...suggesting that anything 
that gets going will have support for organization. With the 
potential for that boundary to turn zonal this 
afternoon/evening...think upscale growth could be a concern. Deepest 
moisture may end up well to our south, across southern Lower today, 
and we may well tap into some drier air aloft that could limit 
shower/storm activity... but will still be close enough to warrant 
some beefier rainfall totals. 

Better rainfall chances should come tonight into Wednesday as the 
low-level jet strengthens closer to our area, allowing for better 
support of nocturnal convection and moist advection off the zonal 
boundary likely to stall just to our south tonight and slowly drift 
back northward/northeastward Wednesday. Better instability 
parameters may remain near and south of M-72...which could result in 
most, if not all, the stronger storms staying south. However, 
appears we should still have around 40kts deep layer shear to work 
with...and another afternoon of upscale growth potential, with shear 
vectors parallel to the boundary; weak low-level flow again should 
support the idea of lake breezes and potential for localized 
convergence to enhance any storms. Other concern is that pwats
